nodes.label: Agentic Scientific Discovery Survey
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive survey on LLM-based agents for scientific discovery across genomics, protein engineering, medicine, chemistry, materials science, physics, and other domains

nodes.label: Scientific Agents
nodes.rationale: LLM-based autonomous agents designed to conduct scientific discovery by integrating domain-specific tools, executing experiments, and iteratively exploring unknown domains

nodes.label: Reinforcement Learning for Agents
nodes.rationale: RL paradigm for training agents to optimize reasoning and tool execution through verifiable rewards; enables transition from passive text generation to active decision-making

nodes.label: Genomics Domain
nodes.rationale: Scientific domain where agents conduct gene expression analysis, CRISPR design, perturbation studies, and cell-type annotation using specialized tools

nodes.label: Protein Engineering Domain
nodes.rationale: Scientific domain where agents design novel proteins with specific properties using structure prediction, physics-aware simulations, and closed-loop experimental validation

nodes.label: Chemistry Domain
nodes.rationale: Scientific domain where agents design molecules, optimize synthesis conditions, perform retrosynthesis planning, and conduct quantum chemistry calculations

nodes.label: Materials Science Domain
nodes.rationale: Scientific domain where agents discover novel materials through autonomous synthesis, property prediction, and inverse design using computational simulations

nodes.label: AlphaGenome
nodes.rationale: Genome annotation and regulatory function prediction tool used by scientific agents in genomics domain

nodes.label: AlphaFold
nodes.rationale: Protein structure prediction model used by agents for protein design and engineering workflows

nodes.label: Rosetta
nodes.rationale: Versatile library for protein modeling and design used in protein engineering agent workflows

nodes.label: RDKit
nodes.rationale: Cheminformatics library for molecular data processing used by chemistry agents

nodes.label: VASP
nodes.rationale: Quantum chemistry simulation tool used by materials science agents for molecular behavior prediction

nodes.label: SpatialAgent
nodes.rationale: Autonomous agent for spatial biology that processes 2M+ cells across spatial transcriptomics pipelines to annotate tissue niches and map cell-cell interactions

nodes.label: Team of AI-made Scientists (TAIS)
nodes.rationale: Multi-agent framework that simulates researcher roles for genomics analysis including planning, data preprocessing, biomedical research, statistics, and quality review

nodes.label: CRISPR-GPT
nodes.rationale: Agent that automates gene-editing experiment design from system selection to delivery and validation protocols with real-world wet-lab execution

nodes.label: SAMPLE
nodes.rationale: Closed-loop self-driving protein engineering pipeline that experimentally discovers thermostable enzyme variants through autonomous design-build-test cycles in robotic labs

nodes.label: Coscientist
nodes.rationale: Agent that autonomously designs and executes complex physical experiments from high-level prompts, demonstrated on Nobel Prize-winning palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions

nodes.label: ChemCrow
nodes.rationale: Agent equipped with 18 expert-designed chemistry tools for autonomous planning and multi-tool analysis across organic synthesis, drug discovery, and materials science

nodes.label: A-Lab
nodes.rationale: Fully autonomous materials synthesis facility that synthesized 41 novel compounds from 58 targets over 17 days using robotic arms and X-ray diffractometers

nodes.label: Biomni
nodes.rationale: General-purpose biomedical agent that completes end-to-end analyses including causal gene prioritization, drug repurposing, and multi-omics integration using 150+ tools

nodes.label: Environment Problem for Science Agents
nodes.rationale: Challenge that science agents must parse outputs from diverse digital tools with non-standard interfaces and interact with physical laboratory equipment, introducing latency, noise, and irreversibility

nodes.label: Action Problem for Science Agents
nodes.rationale: Challenge that science agents face enormous non-standard action spaces across different tools and must create new tools through code generation, expanding action space to near-infinite

nodes.label: Observation Problem for Science Agents
nodes.rationale: Challenge that science agents must process mixed-modality observations including images, spectrometry data, simulation curves, and unstructured text while maintaining long-term memory

nodes.label: Reward Problem for Science Agents
nodes.rationale: Challenge that scientific discovery has highly sparse rewards over years, ambiguous success criteria, and difficulty measuring novelty and impact—breaking down standard RL reward paradigms

nodes.label: Serendipity in Scientific Discovery
nodes.rationale: Role of chance and unexpected findings in major scientific breakthroughs; LLMs trained on likelihood maximization may struggle to explore randomness needed for serendipitous discoveries

nodes.label: Humanity's Knowledge Closure
nodes.rationale: Boundary of existing human knowledge; LLMs are confined within this closure while scientific agents can break through via physical interaction and experimentation

nodes.label: Autonomous Agents for Scientific Discovery: Orchestrating Scientists, Language, Code, and Physics
nodes.author: Zhou et al.
nodes.rationale: Comprehensive survey of LLM-based scientific agents; proposes information-theoretic framework analyzing entropy/verifiability across hypothesis discovery, experimental design, and result analysis phases.

nodes.label: Hypothesis Discovery Phase
nodes.rationale: First phase of scientific discovery; involves knowledge extraction, hypothesis generation, and screening/validation to identify novel, verifiable hypotheses from data.

nodes.label: Experimental Design & Execution Phase
nodes.rationale: Second phase; translates hypotheses into detailed workflows through tool use and tool creation, bridging abstract plans to physical/computational execution.

nodes.label: Result Analysis & Refinement Phase
nodes.rationale: Third phase; interprets experimental results and enters iterative refinement loops to progressively improve processes and validate findings.

nodes.label: Information Entropy Framework
nodes.rationale: Core analytical framework; quantifies uncertainty in hypothesis space; high entropy in hypothesis discovery, low in tool use; guides understanding of automation difficulty.

nodes.label: Verifiability Property
nodes.rationale: Measures ability of information to be objectively tested; ultimate goal of scientific process is transforming low-verifiability ideas into high-verifiability facts.

nodes.label: Dissipation in Scientific Discovery
nodes.rationale: Unavoidable computational cost of exploring unproductive paths; related to Landauer's Principle; high in hypothesis discovery and tool creation, low in tool use.

nodes.label: Five-Level Autonomy Framework
nodes.rationale: Classifies scientific agents from Level 1 (Human-Led) to Level 5 (Full AI Autonomy); grounded in information-processing capabilities rather than holistic roles.

nodes.label: Knowledge Extraction Methods
nodes.rationale: Cornerstone of hypothesis discovery; includes scientific foundation models, RAG-based approaches, multimodal extraction, and prompt-based methods.

nodes.label: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge
nodes.rationale: Technique to address hallucination and outdated knowledge; connects LLMs to external knowledge sources for factually-grounded, traceable outputs.

nodes.label: Hypothesis Generation Approaches
nodes.rationale: Four main approaches: Prompt-Based, Knowledge-Grounded, Multi-Agent Systems, and Evolutionary Algorithm-Based; each balances novelty, accuracy, and scalability differently.

nodes.label: Multi-Agent Hypothesis Generation
nodes.rationale: Emulates collective brainstorming using diverse agents or roles; generates richer hypothesis pools by activating distinct generative distributions.

nodes.label: Evolutionary Algorithm-Based Hypothesis Generation
nodes.rationale: Treats hypothesis generation as optimization; iteratively refines population using mutation/recombination with fitness functions; navigates vast combinatorial spaces.

nodes.label: Hypothesis Screening & Validation
nodes.rationale: Two approaches: Metric-Based Screening (automated, objective criteria) and Agent-Based Validation (collaborative critique); manages volume of generated ideas.

nodes.label: RAG for Experimental Design
nodes.rationale: Grounds experimental plans in external knowledge; agents query specialized tools, databases, and literature to build scientifically valid plans from established facts.

nodes.label: Tool Use in Scientific Agents
nodes.rationale: Four strategies: Embedded (hard-coded pipelines), Toolbox-Based (agent selects from library), Reflective & Iterative (ReAct loops), Hierarchical (multi-agent delegation).

nodes.label: Tool Creation by Agents
nodes.rationale: Agents generate novel algorithms and tools; represents frontier where AI shifts from application to invention; highest entropy and dissipation phase.

nodes.label: Result Analysis Paradigms
nodes.rationale: Three approaches: Modality-Driven (multimodal perception), Tool-Augmented (external APIs), Computation-Native (code generation); often blended in advanced systems.

nodes.label: Iterative Result Refinement
nodes.rationale: Three strategies: Automatic Self-Correction (introspective refinement), External Evaluation (tool-based validation), Human-in-the-Loop (expert oversight).

nodes.label: Scientific Foundation Models
nodes.rationale: Domain-specific models (BioBERT, BioGPT, Galactica) trained on scientific data; overcome limitations of general models in specialized fields.

nodes.label: Genomics Scientific Agents
nodes.rationale: Domain-specific agents for genomics including SpatialAgent, TAIS, CRISPR-GPT, BioDiscoveryAgent; demonstrate application across genetic analysis and perturbation.

nodes.label: Chemistry Scientific Agents
nodes.rationale: Domain-specific agents including Coscientist, ChemCrow, ChemAgents; demonstrate application to drug discovery, materials synthesis, and reaction optimization.

nodes.label: Materials Science Agents
nodes.rationale: Domain-specific agents including A-Lab, ChatMOF, LLMatDesign; demonstrate application to crystal structure discovery and materials design.

nodes.label: Protein Science Agents
nodes.rationale: Domain-specific agents including SAMPLE, Virtual Lab, ProtAgents; demonstrate application to protein design and antibody engineering.

nodes.label: Physics Scientific Agents
nodes.rationale: Domain-specific agents including k-agents, AtomAgents, Mephisto; demonstrate application to quantum computing and fluid dynamics.
